newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down due to share price jump.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down due to share price jump.

text.p: The key September three-month Euroyen futures contract ended down on Monday, as Tokyo share prices surged in the afternoon.
Traders who bought Euroyen futures when stock prices tumbled on Friday moved to liquidate their long positions, a trader for a brokerage house said.
"I don't think new short positions have been built today," the trader added.

The trader said he did not believe Tokyo share prices had yet confirmed a floor, despite a sharp rise in the Nikkei 225 average on Monday afternoon, and a further fall in share prices might lead to gains in the September Euroyen futures contract.

In the Tokyo stock market, the Nikkei 225 average soared 815.14 points or 4.71 percent to finish at 18,118.79. The Nikkei fell more than 2,000 points last week on worries about the economy and the health of financial institutions.
Some said a further fall in the stock market could lead to speculation that the Bank of Japan may take measures to counter the recent trend of plummeting share prices.

If stock prices were to fall to 16,000 yen, it could lead to speculation that the BOJ might temporarily provide increased liquidity to the money market, which could trigger a rise in Euroyen futures, a trader for a long-term credit bank said.
If such speculation grew, the September could make a try for 99.40, the first trader said.

A city bank trader said, however, that the recent weakness in the stock market had had little effect on short-term interest rates, since it was almost unthinkable that the BOJ would make any change in its monetary policy.
